children: Bank Nifty index fell for third straight session on September 8 and was trading below the 57,000-mark with ICICI Bank, Axis Bank among top Nifty losers.
At 12 pm on September 8, Bank Nifty was trading 0.4% lower at 56,865.85 with Axis Bank, ICICI Bank leading the losses by trading 1.8% and 1.7% lower, respectively.
Other losers on the sectoral index were Union Bank of India, HDFC Bank, which were trading 1.2% and 0.9% lower, respectively.

"Index in the immediate short term is seen trading in the range of 57,000-58,000 levels. A close below 57,000 will signal extension of decline towards the key short-term support area of 56,500-56,200 levels being the confluence of the 52 weeks EMA and the lower band of the last 9 weeks range. Overall, the broader 9 weeks consolidation range remains intact between 56,500 and 58,700," said Pabitro Mukherjee, Deputy Vice President-Research, Bajaj Broking.

"Bank Nifty formed a bearish candlestick on the daily chart and closed near its crucial support zone. The index has decisively slipped below its 20-DMA and 200-DMA, indicating a weak short-term technical structure. However, it continues to hold above the key 57,000 level. A sustained move below 57,000 could trigger further downside towards 56,000. Conversely, holding above 57,000 may keep the index range-bound between 57,000 and 58,000. Immediate support is placed at 56,900–57,000, while resistance is seen at 57,900–58,000," said Vatsal Bhuva, Technical Analyst at LKP Securities.

"The immediate support is placed at 56,800, followed by 56,620. On the upside, 57,400 serves as key resistance, followed by 57,500. The index continues to lean weaker, and unless the resistance zone is decisively taken out, the short-term trend remains weak, warranting a cautious approach," said Om Mehra, Technical Research Analyst, SAMCO Securities.

title: Bank Nifty falls for third session, trades below 57k; ICICI, Axis Bank top Nifty losers: What lies ahead?
